findings.pitch: The whole solid-apps suite loads its auth layer from an unpinned, un-SRI'd <script src="https://unpkg.com/xlogin"> (xlogin supplies the credentialed authFetch used for every private-pod read/write), so one hijacked or broken 'latest' publish of xlogin runs with full pod credentials in ~18 apps at once — pin an exact version with an SRI integrity hash, or vendor the file the way intents does.
findings.evidence: Unversioned, integrity-less `<script src="https://unpkg.com/xlogin">` in index.html across the suite: notifications, camera, gallery, webacl, tunnel, peer, wallet, health, nutrition (batch I) AND weather, maps, messages, contacts, kanban, bookmarks, notes, calendar, split (batch J); taproot loads it too. maps also pulls leaflet@1.9.4 and taproot qrcodejs from CDN without SRI. intents is the only app that vendors it.

findings.pitch: nexus's HTML/markdown sanitizer strips script/style/iframe tags but leaves inline event-handler attributes (onerror/onclick) and javascript: URLs intact before assigning doc.body.innerHTML, so any fetched web page or pod document (e.g. ) executes JS in the app origin with the user's authenticated fetch (which can PUT to the pod) — strip on* attributes and javascript: hrefs in the same sanitize pass.
